implReport.summary: All 36 tier-B or second-hand audio files (26 archive.org plus 10 OpenGameArt) are replaced under the same ids by original sounds from deterministic renderers in tools/audio/. The renderers use seeded noise, filters, envelopes, modal resonators and Doppler, with no input recordings, and ffmpeg libmp3lame encodes at the old 96 kbps / 44.1 kHz and layouts. Nine OpenGameArt files stay (author's own page, CC0 badge, not on the integrator's list); their evidence is the recorded page badge only, which is residual risk. No first-hand source was recorded because the network was not used. Loops are periodic by construction, so the wrap is exact. Measurements are on the decoded MP3: beds -24.0 / -26.0 / -22.0 LUFS, true peak -3.0 dBFS or lower. Nobody can listen here, so a person's ear check is still advisable. src/audio tests pass (220 passed, 1 skipped); the LONG provenance test passes and compares shipped files with a fresh render. One test outside my paths now fails: src/ui/screens/credits/parse.test.ts line 25 still expects an 'archive.org' credits group, so the UI owner needs a one-line change.

findings.title: The always-on provenance test fails in the implementer's own paths (level-match slack contradicts the encoder compensation)
findings.detail: renderPcm lowers a level-matched one-shot only to old meanLufs + 0.45 dB, counting on the encoder to take off about 0.45 dB. checkSpec(..., { encode: false }) compares that PCM with old + 0.3. So every one-shot that is level-matched rather than peak-limited fails by construction. Reproduce: `npx vitest run src/audio/provenance.test.ts` gives 'audio/sfx/ui_click_01: mean -25.1 LUFS louder than the file it replaces (-25.6)'. Run without the encoder, 21 of the 28 one-shots fail the same way (water_drip_02 in the cheap list is one). pipeline.mjs (mtime 04:57) was changed after the test file (04:54). The report's '220 passed' does not hold on the tree. Fix: make the PCM-only check allow ENCODER_LOSS_DB, or judge the cheap set on the encoded file.

findings.title: The new MP3s have no Xing/Info (LAME) gapless header, so decoders keep the encoder delay and padding
findings.detail: ffmpeg cannot seek back on a pipe, so the mp3 muxer leaves out the Info frame. The old files and the nine kept ones carry it ('Info' ... 'Lavc60.31' at byte 0x24). In Chrome's decodeAudioData the old crickets_night is 1984500 samples (exact) and the new one 1986048. ui_click_01 is 6912 samples against 4851 rendered; the old click was 4088. thud_giant_step_01 starts sounding at sample 1118 against 224 in the old file. Effects: (a) every replaced one-shot (UI clicks, giant steps, drips, chirps, car passes) plays about 20-25 ms late, which matters for UI feedback and for thuds synced to footfalls; (b) a random-offset slice (gravel step slices of 30-80 ms, dig-bite) can fall in the silent lead-in; (c) a plain loop=true of any new loop has a hard silent gap (analyse.mjs: naive rmsDipRatio 0 for all 8 new loops), so 'periodic by construction, the wrap is exact' holds for the PCM, not for the shipped file; (d) the records' `seconds` (ffprobe) reads 0.16 s for a 0.11 s click. The game's crossfading loop player hides (c), so the beds play fine (analyse: all loops ok). Fix: encode to a temporary seekable file and read it back. A scratch run gave the Info tag and identical bytes on two runs. Demonstrated by two failing tests in src/audio/provenance.verify.test.ts.

findings.title: The one-shot loudness metric counts encoder delay and padding, so the report blames the -3 dBFS peak for the wrong sounds
findings.where: tools/audio/check.mjs:59-61; tools/audio/measure.ts:26-46; docs/design/tasks/audio-provenance-report.md (one-shot table, the 'could not match under the -3 dBFS peak' list)
findings.detail: meanLufs is averaged over the whole decoded buffer, which now includes about 1548-2061 samples of delay and padding (finding 2). For a 0.11 s click that alone lowers the reading by about 1.5 LU. ui_click_01 reads -27.1 against an old -25.6, but its true peak is -8.6 dBFS, so the peak did not limit it. The same applies to ui_click_02 (-12.9 dBFS) and ui_hover_01 (-12.7 dBFS), which the report also lists as 'could not match under the -3 dBFS peak'. ENCODER_LOSS_DB = 0.45 was tuned against this skewed reading. Measure only the content (skip the delay, cut to the rendered length), or fix finding 2 first.

findings.title: The report's 'before' seam and join numbers use a window shifted by 1105 samples on the old files
findings.detail: The old files carry the Info tag, so ffmpeg and Chrome already strip their delay. measure.ts still slices [1105, 1105 + content), which shifts and truncates the old loop. Reported old traffic_distant jump/kink: 15.3 / 138.3. On the correct window [0, content) they are 2.83 / 28.2. For crickets_night: 1.03 / 1.8 reported against 0.11 / 0.43. The 'after' column is right. The before/after comparison in the report overstates how bad the old seams were.

findings.title: The nine kept OpenGameArt files are labelled tier 'A' without the evidence the spec's tier A needs
findings.where: tools/audio/sync-records.mjs:48-50 (r.tier = 'A' for every kept file); assets-src/records_audio.json
findings.detail: The spec defines tier A as 'first-hand source with a licence the repository can show'. For the nine kept files the repository holds only a recorded badge string, with no saved page or licence text; the audit itself calls this 'residual risk'. Criterion 1 is still met, because those files were never on the audit's 'cannot be shown' list. But the machine-readable label says more than the evidence supports. A separate value such as tier 'A-badge' or `evidence: 'page badge recorded 2026-11-12, no saved copy'` would keep the records honest. The provenance test also asserts tier A for all 45 records.
